_comment: Railways (core rg/rail_meshes.h, RACE-028): what the served g2m.rail.geom layer looks like and when a rail bridge has collision. All [AS] (assumed, typical single-track German main line: Ril 804 bridge cross-sections) except the standard gauge. Units metres. sample_spacing_m = longest step along a piece; max_tracks_drawn caps a piece tagged with more tracks; the profile height of a piece is the top of the ballast.

draw._comment: classes by name (rail, light_rail, subway, tram); tunnels are never drawn (no portals in v1), subway and tram are off (street surface / tunnel). construction = railway=construction pieces (deck and ballast always, rails only with construction_rails). declined = pieces the layer could not profile.

bridge._comment: Single-track deck (+ track_spacing_m per extra track): slab under a ballast trough, parapets at both edges rising parapet_height_m above the track bed.

bed._comment: Ballast trapezoid: ballast_top_width_m wide at the profile height (+ track_spacing_m per extra track); on a deck ballast_height_m thick, on the ground it reaches ballast_depth_m below the profile into the terrain; side slope = horizontal metres per vertical metre.

collision._comment: A bridge piece gets a slab collider (deck + ballast) only over the spans whose underside is at least min_clearance_m above the ground there (probed at the centre and edge_margin_m inside both edges): a rail deck must never block the road under it - a span with less clearance keeps its look, a vehicle drives through it. unknown_ground_blocks false: where no ground height is known the span has no collision either. Rails, ballast beds on the ground and parapets have no collision in v1.
